videos.description:
In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, I revisit episode 2 of my six-part guest series with Dr. Andy Galpin, PhD, an exercise scientist and expert in human performance. We discuss how strength and muscle growth (hypertrophy) differ and why resistance training is important for maintaining physical function as we age. We also explain how to build effective training programs using progressive overload, exercise selection, repetition speed and weekly training volume. Dr. Galpin shares practical tools for developing strength, power and muscle size, including how to adapt workouts to your goals, equipment and schedule.

Laya AI — A Different Kind of AI Model

Laya is a multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine. Instead of generating long text like a traditional LLM, it is designed to take an input and make structured decisions such as choice, score, and yes/no-style probability decisions in a single forward pass.

33ms Decision Making

One of Laya’s headline claims is speed. The project reports about 32.8–33 ms for a single multilingual question on an NVIDIA T4 GPU, with batched workloads reaching roughly 7.2 ms per question for 10 questions. These figures are hardware- and workload-specific benchmark results, rather than a guaranteed latency on every machine.

100+ Languages

Laya includes a dedicated multilingual checkpoint based on mmBERT, and its router can detect the language/script and route non-English requests to that model. The project describes support for 100+ languages, making multilingual decision workflows one of its key differentiators.

Decisions, Not Text Generation

This is the important difference: Laya isn't trying to replace a general-purpose LLM. It focuses on decisions over existing information. For example, you could give it a customer-support ticket and ask which department should receive it, how urgent it is, or whether the customer shows churn risk. Because the output is structured rather than free-form generated text, it can be useful as a decision/routing layer inside AI systems.

Run Locally & Self-Host

Laya can be installed locally through Python and also provides a self-hosted HTTP server, Docker support, an optional MCP server, ONNX support, and integrations for LangChain/LangGraph. This means developers can deploy it inside their own infrastructure instead of depending exclusively on a hosted model API.

Open Source & Self-Hosted Cost

The repository is released under the Apache 2.0 license, and its benchmark comparison describes the model itself as $0 self-hosted versus usage-priced hosted APIs. Of course, “zero cost” here means no model/API usage fee; running it still requires your own CPU/GPU, electricity, or cloud infrastructure.

Why Laya is Interesting

The interesting idea behind Laya is combining fast structured decisions + multilingual support + local deployment. Instead of using a large generative model for every classification, routing, scoring, moderation, triage, or guardrail decision, Laya is designed specifically for these narrower decision tasks.
